Ringed wormholes only spawn from 1,000 light-years and flower-aura wormholes from 2,500 (Serebii's spawn table, Bulbapedia's N/A cells). Below those distances this model shows what the datamined formula would give: 1% for one or two rings, 4/8/12% for a flower aura at 1,000–2,499 light-years, and — because 0% cannot be shown — the 1% default for a flower aura below 1,000 light-years, where the formula gives 0%.
Only one Pokémon appears per visit, and every Pokémon found in the Ultra Space Wilds has at least three perfect IVs.

games.name: Let's Go, Pikachu! / Let's Go, Eevee!

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild spawns without a Catch Combo: 1/4096; a Lure adds 1 roll and the Shiny Charm 2.
methods.details: Every wild Pokémon rolls for Shiny when it spawns: once normally, plus one roll while a Lure, Super Lure or Max Lure is active and two more with the Shiny Charm. This is also what every spawn gets when you have no Catch Combo, or when it is not the species you are chaining. Count each spawn of your target as one encounter.

inputs.label: Lure active
inputs.description: On while a Lure (100 steps), Super Lure (200 steps) or Max Lure (250 steps) is in effect: +1 Shiny roll.

notes: Lures, the Shiny Charm and Catch Combos have no effect on gift Pokémon or in-game trades: the Alolan-form trades, gifts such as Arcanine/Persian and the revived fossils always get the single 1/4096 roll (SerebiiNet's December 2018 update).
A Catch Combo on a different species gives nothing here: in Anubis' test at a Bellsprout combo of 31, every Pidgey spawned with only the Lure and Charm rolls.

Interactable encounters (the road-blocking Snorlax, the legendary birds in their original locations and Mewtwo): RotomLabs lists them at 1/4096, or 1/1365.67 with the Shiny Charm, and says only the charm boosts them — leave the Lure toggle off for those. This is community-sourced; no datamine write-up confirming it was found for this file.
Serebii prints these as 1/2048, 1/1365.3 and 1/1024 (straight multiples of 1/4096); the exact values for independent rolls are 1/2048.25, 1/1365.67 and 1/1024.38, as in Anubis' table.

methods.name: Catch Combo
methods.summary: Catch one species in a row: +3 rolls from a combo of 11, +7 from 21, +11 from 31 (up to 1/273.53).
methods.details: Catch the same species over and over to build a Catch Combo. At a combo of 11–20 the next spawn of that species gets 3 extra Shiny rolls, 7 at 21–30 and 11 from 31 upward; an active Lure adds 1 and the Shiny Charm 2, for a maximum of 15 rolls. The combo bonus is spent on the very next spawn of the chained species after each catch, so keep catching to re-arm it rather than standing still and waiting.

inputs.label: Catch Combo
inputs.description: Current combo shown on screen for the species you are chaining. Nothing changes for Shiny odds after 31.

inputs.label: Lure active
inputs.description: On while a Lure (100 steps), Super Lure (200 steps) or Max Lure (250 steps) is in effect: +1 Shiny roll.

notes: The combo rolls apply only once, to the very next spawn of the chained species after a catch (Anubis / Sibuna_Switch, 2022). If you idle after reaching 31, that first spawn gets the bonus and everything after it, including more of the chained species, only gets the base, Lure and Shiny Charm rolls (see Full odds). The originally datamined roll counts were correct; only the idling strategy was wrong.
Spawns of any other species never get the combo rolls.

The combo breaks if a wild Pokémon flees, if you catch a different species (even from the same evolutionary line) or if you close the game. Running away yourself or moving to another route or city does not break it.
Longer combos make wild Pokémon flee more readily: the starting flee value of 242 is reduced by twice the combo length (Bulbapedia).
Catch Combos, Lures and the Shiny Charm do nothing for gift Pokémon or in-game trades.

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild encounters and overworld static Pokémon: 1/4096, or 3 rolls (1/1365.67) with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Every wild encounter slot (overworld symbols, fishing spots, hidden "!" grass and berry trees), the daily strong spawns of the Wild Area and overworld static Pokémon such as the Swords of Justice make one Shiny roll; the Shiny Charm adds 2 more. Overworld models never look Shiny, so you only find out once the battle starts. A Pokémon's shininess is decided when it spawns: saving next to a visible Pokémon or fishing spot and reloading brings back the same Pokémon, so keep generating new spawns instead. For the Swords of Justice, run from the battle, stand on the spawn point, then enter and leave your camp (or save and restart the game) so that a fresh one is generated.
notes: Not affected by the Shiny Charm (always 1/4096): Max Raid Battles, the Regis, the Motostoke Gym Pokémon, the Glimwood Tangle Impidimp, curry visitors, revived fossils, Regina's trades and other gift Pokémon (RotomLabs, Smogon, Bulbapedia). Use the Max Raid Battles or Scripted encounters entries for these.
Eggs do not get the 3-roll charm figure: an Egg from same-language parents gets only 2 rolls with the charm. Use the Breeding or Masuda Method entries for Eggs.
Overworld spawns and fishing spots are generated with their shininess already decided, so soft resetting next to a visible spawn never changes it (Smogon).

Wild Pokémon above your current capture level (the "very strong-looking" ones you cannot catch yet) are forced to be non-Shiny (Serebii, RotomLabs; the decompiled spawn routine checks the level cap before rolling).

Shiny-locked: Zacian, Zamazenta, Eternatus, Calyrex, Glastrier, Spectrier, Keldeo and the Galarian Articuno, Zapdos and Moltres; gift Pokémon such as the Galar starters, the gift Charmander and the other Kanto starters that can Gigantamax, Type: Null, Toxel, Cosmog, Kubfu, Poipole, Porygon, the Alolan-form rewards of the Diglett quest and the Gigantamax Pikachu and Eevee; the Galarian Slowpoke at Wedgehurst Station and the Route 3 Corvisquire; NPC trades on the Galar mainland (RotomLabs, Smogon).
Serebii prints the charm rate as 1 in 1365.33 (3/4096); the exact 3-roll value is 1/1365.67.

methods.name: Breeding (same language)
methods.summary: Eggs from same-language parents: 1/4096, or only 2 rolls (1/2048.25) with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Hatch Eggs from two parents that come from games of the same language. Without the Shiny Charm an Egg makes a single Shiny roll. With the charm the Egg gets the charm's 2 rerolls but loses its ordinary first roll, so it ends up with 2 rolls instead of the 3 that wild encounters get. Count one encounter per Egg.
notes: The charm case is exactly 2 rolls: 1 - (4095/4096)^2 = 8191/16777216.

Source disagreement: Serebii and many guides quote the charm as 1 in 1365 without separating Eggs. RotomLabs' Egg table, Bulbapedia (citing SciresM) and the reverse-engineered Egg routine (rerolls = 6 if Masuda, +2 if charm, and the ordinary first roll is skipped whenever a reroll is active) give 2 rolls for charm-only Eggs. The code-level behaviour is used here.
Switching to a foreign-language parent (Masuda Method) is about six times better without the charm and about four times better with it.

methods.name: Masuda Method
methods.summary: Eggs from parents of different languages: 6 rolls (1/683.08), 8 with the Shiny Charm (1/512.44).
methods.details: Leave two compatible Pokémon whose games of origin have different languages at a Nursery and collect the Eggs. For such a pair the game makes 6 Shiny rolls per Egg instead of 1, and the Shiny Charm adds 2 more. Count one encounter per Egg; the shininess of an Egg is decided when you receive it, not when it hatches.
notes: In the Egg routine the Masuda Method grants 6 rerolls and the Shiny Charm 2, and the ordinary first roll is skipped whenever any reroll is active, so the totals are 6 and 8 rolls rather than 7 and 9 (PyNXReader Egg code; RotomLabs Egg table; Bulbapedia, citing SciresM).
Egg shininess is determined when the Egg is received, not when it hatches (Smogon).
Serebii rounds these to 1 in 682.7 and 1 in 512 (6/4096 and 8/4096); the exact values are 1/683.08 and 1/512.44.

methods.name: Number Battled (KO method)
methods.summary: Raise a species' Number Battled: 1.5–3% of its spawns are Brilliant and get 1–6 extra Shiny rolls.
methods.details: Knock out or catch the target species to raise its Number Battled in the Pokédex, then keep battling its visible overworld spawns. Each spawn first rolls for a Brilliant aura (1.5% from 1 battled, 2% from 20, 2.5% from 50, 3% from 100) and only Brilliant spawns receive the extra Shiny rolls: +1 from 1 battled, +2 from 50, +3 from 100, +4 from 200, +5 from 300 and +6 from 500. The odds shown are the average over every spawn of the species, Brilliant or not. After a KO there is a 50% chance that the next spawn is the same species, which speeds up the hunt.

inputs.label: Number Battled
inputs.description: The "Number Battled" shown on the species' Pokédex page. It rises each time you knock out or catch the species. The bonus stops growing at 500.

bonuses.label: Brilliant aura, 1–19 battled (+1 roll on 1.5% of spawns)
Brilliant aura, 20–49 battled (+1 roll on 2% of spawns)
Brilliant aura, 50–99 battled (+2 rolls on 2.5% of spawns)
Brilliant aura, 100+ battled (+3 to +6 rolls on 3% of spawns)

notes: The widely quoted 1/585.57 (1/455.56 with the charm) at 500 battled only applies to spawns that are Brilliant. Averaged over all spawns the method is worth about 1/3472 without and 1/1288 with the Shiny Charm at 500 battled — barely better than plain charm odds (1/1365.67).
The averaged figures are derived here from the decompiled brilliant rates and roll counts; the sources only print the odds of a spawn that is already Brilliant.

Every source agrees that the extra rolls belong to Brilliant Pokémon only: Serebii heads its table "Brilliant Aura Pokémon", Bulbapedia states that non-Brilliant Pokémon have no enhanced Shiny rate, RotomLabs lists non-Brilliant spawns at 1 roll (3 with the charm) for every KO count, and the decompiled spawn routine (Lincoln-LM) adds the bonus rolls only when the 1.5–3% brilliant roll succeeds.
Nothing breaks the bonus: Number Battled never goes down and there is no chain to keep alive.
Number Battled also rises when the species is defeated in Max Raid Battles and Trainer battles, but not in link battles, the Battle Tower or Restricted Sparring (Bulbapedia).

Hidden "!" grass encounters, strong Wild Area spawns and static Pokémon never roll for a Brilliant aura, so they get no bonus (Smogon; the decompiled routine only allows Brilliant spawns for non-hidden encounter slots).
The brilliant rate stops improving at 100 battled (3%); further KOs only add rolls for the spawns that are Brilliant.
When fishing with a streak, use the Chain fishing entry: the streak raises the Brilliant chance.

methods.name: Brilliant aura spawn
methods.summary: A spawn already showing the Brilliant aura: 2–7 rolls by Number Battled (1/2048.25 to 1/585.57).
methods.details: Use this when you only count spawns of the target that show the Brilliant aura particle effect. A Brilliant Pokémon gets 1 extra Shiny roll from 1 battled, 2 from 50, 3 from 100, 4 from 200, 5 from 300 and 6 from 500, on top of the base roll and the Shiny Charm's 2 rolls. These are the per-Pokémon figures printed in most guides.

inputs.label: Number Battled
inputs.description: The "Number Battled" shown on the species' Pokédex page. It rises each time you knock out or catch the species. At least 1 is needed for Brilliant spawns; the bonus stops growing at 500.

notes: Only 1.5–3% of overworld spawns are Brilliant (up to 28% with a fishing streak of 25 or more). For the average odds per spawn use the Number Battled or Chain fishing entries.
The 20-battled step raises the chance of a Brilliant spawn (1.5% to 2%) but not its roll count.
Serebii prints 1 in 1024.8 for 100 battled without the charm; the exact 4-roll value is 1/1024.38 (RotomLabs).
Brilliant Pokémon also have 2–3 guaranteed perfect IVs, know an Egg Move, are the highest level of their encounter slot and award Watts (Smogon, Serebii).
If several Brilliant Pokémon are on screen, only the one closest to the player shows the particle effect (Smogon).

methods.name: Chain fishing (Brilliant streak)
methods.summary: A fishing streak raises the Brilliant chance by up to 25 points; Brilliant Pokémon get bonus rolls.
methods.details: Fish repeatedly in the same area and knock out everything you reel in; the streak counts every fishing encounter, whatever the species. A streak of 3–6 consecutive fishing encounters adds 2 percentage points to the Brilliant chance, 7–14 adds 5, 15–24 adds 10 and 25 or more adds 25, on top of the 1.5–3% that comes from the species' Number Battled. Only Brilliant Pokémon receive the extra Shiny rolls (1–6, by Number Battled), so raise the target's Number Battled first. The odds shown are the average per fishing encounter with the target species.

inputs.label: Number Battled
inputs.description: The "Number Battled" shown on the species' Pokédex page. It rises each time you knock out or catch the species. The bonus stops growing at 500.

inputs.label: Fishing streak
inputs.description: Consecutive fishing encounters (any species) reeled in and knocked out without breaking the streak. The bonus stops growing at 25.

model.spec:
Inputs: defeated (integer >= 0, the species' Number Battled), chain (integer >= 0, current fishing streak), shinyCharm (boolean, true only when the Shiny Charm is on and applies).
Constants: D = params.denominator = 4096; charmRolls = params.charmRolls = 2.
1. Look up (brilliantPermille, bonusRolls) from defeated, first match wins: defeated >= 500 -> (30, 6); >= 300 -> (30, 5); >= 200 -> (30, 4); >= 100 -> (30, 3); >= 50 -> (25, 2); >= 20 -> (20, 1); >= 1 -> (15, 1); otherwise (0, 0).
2. Look up chainPermille from chain, first match wins: chain >= 25 -> 250; >= 15 -> 100; >= 7 -> 50; >= 3 -> 20; otherwise 0.
3. brilliantChance = (defeated >= 1) ? (brilliantPermille + chainPermille) / 1000 : 0. (The game draws a random integer 0-999 and the spawn is Brilliant when brilliantPermille + chainPermille is greater than it; with defeated = 0 the check is skipped entirely.)
4. baseRolls = 1 + (shinyCharm ? charmRolls : 0).
5. q = (D - 1) / D.
6. pNormal = 1 - q^baseRolls. pBrilliant = 1 - q^(baseRolls + bonusRolls).
7. Return p = (1 - brilliantChance) * pNormal + brilliantChance * pBrilliant, the probability that one fishing encounter with the species is shiny.

notes: The streak counts consecutive fishing encounters that you reel in and knock out, regardless of species. It is broken, and the rate resets, if you fail to reel a Pokémon in, catch it, run away, leave the area or turn off the game (Bulbapedia, Serebii).

The Brilliant chance is code-backed: Lincoln-LM's decompilation of the spawn routine adds 20, 50, 100 or 250 (out of 1000) to the Number Battled threshold at streaks of 3, 7, 15 and 25, which matches Bulbapedia and the table in the Smogon guide (Anubis' revision of Kaphotics's table).
Derived figures: the sources publish the Brilliant chance and the Shiny odds of a Brilliant spawn. The averaged odds shown here combine the two and are not printed by any source.
A reply in the Smogon thread says the last two columns of Kaphotics's original table were slightly off; the revised grid (26.5–28% at a streak of 25 or more) is used here.

Source disagreement: Serebii expresses the streak bonus as multipliers (x1.3, x3.3, x6.6, x16.6). Applied to the 1.5% starting rate they give 2%, 5%, 10% and 25% as the whole Brilliant chance, whereas the game code, Bulbapedia and Smogon add those amounts to the Number Battled rate (for example 1.5% + 25% = 26.5%). The additive, code-level behaviour is used here.
A species with 0 battled cannot be Brilliant, so the streak does nothing for it.

methods.name: Dynamax Adventures
methods.summary: Crown Tundra Max Lair: every Pokémon you catch is a flat 1/300, or 1/100 with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Run Dynamax Adventures in the Max Lair (Crown Tundra DLC), catching the Pokémon along the way and the Legendary at the end; the catch rate is always 100%. Each Pokémon you caught has its own flat Shiny chance, and whether it is Shiny is only revealed on the results screen where you pick the one to keep. Count one encounter per Pokémon checked (normally the Legendary).
notes: These odds are flat and cannot be improved by anything other than the Shiny Charm (Serebii). With the charm the game uses exactly 3/300 (Bulbapedia, citing SciresM).

Every Pokémon caught during the run rolls separately, so with four catches the chance that at least one is Shiny is about 1/75.4 without and 1/25.4 with the charm; there is no extra bonus for catching all four (RotomLabs).

Shininess is decided per player on the results screen where you choose the Pokémon to keep, so nothing looks Shiny during the battles and the same Pokémon can be Shiny for one player and not for another (Serebii, RotomLabs).
Each Legendary can only be kept once per save; if you do not take it you can return to it later (Serebii).
Shiny Pokémon from Dynamax Adventures are always star Shinies, never square (Smogon, Bulbapedia).

methods.name: Max Raid Battles
methods.summary: Pokémon in Max Raid dens: a flat 1/4096 — the Shiny Charm does not apply.
methods.details: Every Pokémon occupying a Max Raid den has a flat 1/4096 chance of being Shiny, with or without the Shiny Charm. Whether it is Shiny is decided when the den becomes active and does not change if you reset the game; for a den activated with a Wishing Piece the result of every following day is predetermined as well. Count one encounter per den Pokémon you check.

checkpoints.label: Max Raid Battle, Shiny Charm has no effect

notes: Not affected by the Shiny Charm (RotomLabs, Smogon, Bulbapedia).
Soft resetting does not re-roll a den: its Pokémon is fixed once the den is active (RotomLabs, Bulbapedia).
A raid Pokémon whose level is too high for the host's number of Gym Badges is forced to be non-Shiny (Bulbapedia, Smogon).
Some Wild Area News events featured a 5-star raid with a guaranteed Shiny Pokémon; those are always square Shinies (Bulbapedia, Smogon).
Dynamax Adventures in the Max Lair use different odds — see that entry.

methods.name: Scripted encounters (Regis, fossils, curry)
methods.summary: Regis, fossils, curry visitors, Regina's trades: a flat 1/4096 — the Shiny Charm does not apply.
methods.details: These encounters always make a single Shiny roll, whether or not you own the Shiny Charm. For Regirock, Regice, Registeel and Regieleki or Regidrago, solve the temple puzzle, save in front of the statue that starts the battle and soft reset; for Regigigas, save before interacting with its den. The Motostoke Gym Pokémon and the Glimwood Tangle Impidimp can be hunted the same way by saving next to them. Regina's trade Pokémon already show as Shiny during the trade, so save next to her and retry. Fossils revived by Cara Liss on Route 6 and Pokémon attracted by cooking curry at a camp belong to this group too.

checkpoints.label: Scripted encounter, Shiny Charm has no effect

notes: Smogon's guide marks none of these encounters as affected by the Shiny Charm; RotomLabs lists the Regis, gifts (including Cara Liss's fossils), Regina's trades and curry spawns at 1 roll with or without the charm; Bulbapedia lists the legendary giants, the Motostoke Stadium Pokémon, revived fossils, curry encounters and scripted encounters such as the Glimwood Tangle Impidimp as unaffected.
Regieleki and Regidrago share a temple and only one of them can be caught per save file (Smogon).
Not in this group: the Swords of Justice, strong spawns and one-time overworld encounters such as the Route 5 Eldegoss do get the Shiny Charm — use Full odds for them (RotomLabs, Smogon).
Many gift Pokémon are Shiny-locked; see the notes of the Full odds entry.

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild and static encounters: a flat 1/4096 — in BDSP the Shiny Charm does not affect them.
methods.details: Random wild encounters and static encounters make a single Shiny roll. Unlike other games, the Shiny Charm in BDSP only works for Eggs, so it does not change these odds. For static targets save in front of them and soft reset; for wild targets simply keep encountering.
notes: The Shiny Charm only affects breeding in BDSP. Wild encounters, static encounters, the Poké Radar and the Grand Underground ignore it (Serebii, RotomLabs, Bulbapedia; PokeFinder's BDSP wild and static generators make a single PID roll).
Shiny-locked: the gift Mew and Jirachi in Floaroma Town and Mystery Gift distributions. Every other Pokémon, including the starters, Legendaries and Mythicals, can be Shiny (Serebii, RotomLabs).
RotomLabs states that its rates apply to version 1.1.1 and later.

methods.name: Breeding (same language)
methods.summary: Eggs from same-language parents: 1/4096, or only 2 rolls (1/2048.25) with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Hatch Eggs from two parents that come from games of the same language. Without the Shiny Charm an Egg makes a single Shiny roll. With the charm the Egg gets the charm's 2 rolls but loses its ordinary first roll, so it ends up with 2 rolls. Count one encounter per Egg.
notes: The charm case is exactly 2 rolls: 1 - (4095/4096)^2 = 8191/16777216.
RotomLabs describes this as a quirk (or bug) that skips a Shiny roll when any bonus is active; PokeFinder's Egg generator likewise only rolls the bonus PIDs (6 for Masuda, 2 for the charm).

Source disagreement: PokéCommunity's launch guide says the charm gives Eggs three rolls rather than one, and Serebii only quotes the Masuda figures. RotomLabs (Anubis' data), Bulbapedia and both reverse-engineered Egg generators give 2 rolls for charm-only Eggs. The code-level behaviour is used here.
Switching to a foreign-language parent (Masuda Method) is about six times better without the charm and about four times better with it.

methods.name: Masuda Method
methods.summary: Eggs from parents of different languages: 6 rolls (1/683.08), 8 with the Shiny Charm (1/512.44).
methods.details: Leave two compatible Pokémon whose games of origin have different languages at the Nursery and hatch the Eggs. For such a pair the game makes 6 Shiny rolls per Egg instead of 1, and the Shiny Charm — which in BDSP only works for Eggs — adds 2 more. Count one encounter per Egg.
notes: In the Egg routine the Masuda Method grants 6 PID rolls and the Shiny Charm 2, and the ordinary first roll is skipped whenever a bonus is active, so the totals are 6 and 8 rolls rather than 7 and 9 (PokeFinder EggGenerator8; RotomLabs; Bulbapedia).
Breeding is the only thing the Shiny Charm improves in BDSP.
Serebii rounds these to 1 in 682.7 and 1 in 512 (6/4096 and 8/4096); the exact values are 1/683.08 and 1/512.44.

methods.name: Poké Radar chaining
methods.summary: Chain one species with the Poké Radar: up to 1/99 per patch at a chain of 40.
methods.details: Use the Poké Radar in tall grass with a Repel active: up to four patches of grass shake. Enter one, defeat or catch the Pokémon, and keep entering shaking patches to build a chain of that species. Each shaking patch has the listed chance of being a sparkling Shiny patch for your current chain, and the odds stop improving at a chain of 40. Patches four tiles away are the safest for keeping the chain: Serebii lists an 83% (defeat) or 93% (capture) chance of continuing from the furthest patches against 53% or 63% from the nearest. With a long chain you can also stop battling and re-use the Radar each time it recharges (50 steps): that re-rolls the patches without changing the chain, until one of them sparkles.

inputs.label: Chain length
inputs.description: Current Poké Radar chain. The odds stop improving at 40.

notes: The odds are per shaking patch, not per Radar use (Serebii: "1 in 99 chance for each patch of grass"). Bulbapedia states that the Radar always generates four patches in BDSP, which makes one Radar use at a chain of 40 about a 3.98% (roughly 1/25) chance of showing a Shiny patch; PokéCommunity describes it as up to four patches.

The Shiny Charm has no effect on the Poké Radar (Serebii, Bulbapedia). RotomLabs notes that the game contains a charm calculation for the Radar that is never used; PokéCommunity tabulates those unused rates.

The chain ends if you run from the battle, get a regular wild encounter before reaching a shaking patch (keep a Repel active), use the bike or leave the route, and it can also break at random after any battle — hence the continue rates above (Serebii, PokéCommunity, Bulbapedia).

Source disagreement: Serebii also lists entering a patch that holds a different species as a way to break the chain, while Bulbapedia says that in BDSP every shaking patch holds the chained species. Neither is code-verified here.
This is not the Diamond/Pearl/Platinum curve: the originals capped at about 1/200 per patch at a chain of 40, while BDSP reaches 1/99, with jumps at chains 30 and 36–40.
Chains above 40 do not improve the Shiny odds further (Serebii and Bulbapedia list 1 in 99 for 40 and for 100).

The table holds the published 1-in-N figures (Serebii, RotomLabs, Bulbapedia and PokéCommunity, which credits Kaphotics and mattyoukhana_). The exact internal rates have not been published as fractions, so an entry can be off by a fraction of a percent.

methods.name: Grand Underground
methods.summary: Pokémon Hideaways: 1/4096, or 2 rolls (1/2048.25) while the Diglett bonus is active.
methods.details: Pokémon in the Hideaways of the Grand Underground make a single Shiny roll. Collecting 40 points from Diglett (1 point each) and Dugtrio (3 points each) in one session starts a 4-minute bonus during which every Hideaway Pokémon gets a second roll. Hideaway Pokémon never look Shiny before the battle starts, and saving in front of one and resetting does not re-roll it — leave the room and come back to respawn them. Collect the points, then check as many Hideaway spawns as you can while the bonus is running.

inputs.label: Diglett bonus active
inputs.description: The 4-minute bonus earned by collecting 40 points of Diglett (1) and Dugtrio (3).

checkpoints.label: Diglett bonus, Shiny Charm has no effect
No bonus, Shiny Charm has no effect

notes: The Shiny Charm does not apply in the Grand Underground: RotomLabs lists 1 roll, or 2 with the Diglett bonus, with or without the charm, and PokeFinder's Underground generator uses 2 PID rolls with the bonus and 1 without.
The bonus lasts 4 minutes and the 40 points must be collected in a single session (Serebii).
Serebii quotes the bonus rate as 1 in 2048; the exact 2-roll value is 1/2048.25.
In multiplayer the points are collected, and the bonus is shared, by every player in the same Grand Underground session (Bulbapedia).

Hideaway Pokémon are generated when they spawn: PokéCommunity reports that saving and resetting in front of one does not change whether it is Shiny, while leaving and re-entering the room respawns it.
PokéCommunity mentions a possible extra roll from statues in your Secret Base as unconfirmed; PokeFinder's Underground generator has no such roll, so it is not modelled.

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild spawns: 1 roll, 2 at research level 10, 4 with perfect research; +3 with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Every regular wild spawn makes one Shiny roll at 1/4096. Reaching research level 10 for the species adds 1 roll and a perfect Pokédex page adds 2 more (3 in total); the Shiny Charm adds another 3. Shiny Pokémon are visible in the overworld and a sparkle sound plays when one spawns, so keep re-rolling spawns and listen. You can save in front of a Shiny before trying to catch it.

inputs.label: Research level
inputs.description: The target species' Pokédex research: level 10 adds 1 Shiny roll, a perfect page adds 3 in total.

options.label: Below level 10
options.description: No research bonus. You cannot own the Shiny Charm at this stage: it requires level 10 for every non-Mythical species.

checkpoints.label: Wild spawn, no research bonus (1 roll)
Wild spawn, research level 10 + Shiny Charm (5 rolls)
Wild spawn, perfect research + Shiny Charm (7 rolls)

notes: The Shiny Charm is worth 3 rolls in Legends: Arceus, not the 2 of other games (Serebii; Lincoln-LM's pla-multi-checker).
The charm is awarded for research level 10 on every non-Mythical species (Serebii, Bulbapedia), so in practice you never hold it while a huntable species is still below level 10.

Shiny-locked: every Legendary and Mythical Pokémon (including Phione and Manaphy), the gift starters, the gift Alolan Vulpix and all forced battles in Requests and Missions (RotomLabs, Serebii). The starter species can still be found Shiny in the wild, for example in space-time distortions (Serebii).
Mass Outbreak and Massive Mass Outbreak spawns use much higher roll counts — use those entries for them.

methods.name: Mass Outbreak
methods.summary: Outbreak spawns get 25 extra rolls: 1/158.02, or 1/128.49 with perfect research and the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: As the story progresses you are warned of Mass Outbreaks: four Pokémon of one species gather at one spot and 10–15 appear in total as you catch or defeat them. Every outbreak spawn makes 26 Shiny rolls instead of 1, and the research-level and Shiny Charm rolls are added on top. Count one encounter per outbreak Pokémon checked; returning to Jubilife Village rolls for new outbreaks.

inputs.label: Research level
inputs.description: The target species' Pokédex research: level 10 adds 1 Shiny roll, a perfect page adds 3 in total.

options.label: Below level 10
options.description: No research bonus. You cannot own the Shiny Charm at this stage: it requires level 10 for every non-Mythical species.

checkpoints.label: Mass Outbreak, no research bonus (26 rolls)
Mass Outbreak, research level 10 + Shiny Charm (30 rolls)
Mass Outbreak, perfect research + Shiny Charm (32 rolls)

notes: Serebii prints 1 in 158.2 and 1 in 152.9 for 26 and 27 rolls; the exact values are 1/158.02 and 1/152.19, which is what RotomLabs lists.
The Mass Outbreak and Massive Mass Outbreak bonuses never combine — a spawn belongs to one or the other (RotomLabs).
An outbreak ends once all of its Pokémon have been caught or defeated, and there can be at most one Mass Outbreak per area at a time (Serebii).
Serebii gives each area a 20% chance of generating an outbreak whenever you return to Jubilife Village.
RotomLabs notes that before version 1.1.0 an exploit let you return to Jubilife Village to reset an outbreak for unlimited tries; it has been patched.

methods.name: Massive Mass Outbreak
methods.summary: Storm outbreaks get 12 extra rolls: 1/315.54, or 1/216.05 with perfect research and the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Massive Mass Outbreaks unlock after completing the request "Daybreak" (version 1.1.0) and appear during rainstorms or snowstorms as several outbreaks spread across an area. Each outbreak holds 8–10 Pokémon and can be followed by a second wave of 6–8. Every spawn makes 13 Shiny rolls instead of 1, plus the research-level and Shiny Charm rolls. Giving Mai's Munchlax 5 Aguav Berries at camp reveals the outbreaks on the map.

inputs.label: Research level
inputs.description: The target species' Pokédex research: level 10 adds 1 Shiny roll, a perfect page adds 3 in total.

options.label: Below level 10
options.description: No research bonus. You cannot own the Shiny Charm at this stage: it requires level 10 for every non-Mythical species.

checkpoints.label: Massive Mass Outbreak, no research bonus (13 rolls)
Massive Mass Outbreak, research level 10 (14 rolls)
Massive Mass Outbreak, perfect research (16 rolls)
Massive Mass Outbreak, research level 10 + Shiny Charm (17 rolls)
Massive Mass Outbreak, perfect research + Shiny Charm (19 rolls)

notes: The bonus is 12 extra rolls, lower than a regular Mass Outbreak's 25, because far more Pokémon appear (Serebii).
The outbreaks are tied to the storm: when the weather ends they disappear (Serebii).
The Mass Outbreak and Massive Mass Outbreak bonuses never combine — a spawn belongs to one or the other (RotomLabs).

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild spawns: 1/4096, or 1/1365.67 with the Shiny Charm; Sparkling Power adds up to 3 rolls.
methods.details: Every ordinary wild Pokémon rolls for Shiny when it spawns: once normally, three times with the Shiny Charm. Shiny Pokémon are shown in their Shiny colours in the overworld, but there is no sparkle or sound to alert you, so every spawn has to be checked by eye. Refresh the spawns by walking away and back, crossing a town border, or opening and closing a picnic. A meal with Sparkling Power adds 1 to 3 more rolls for 30 minutes to wild Pokémon of the meal's type; the usual Shiny sandwich is one type-specific ingredient plus two Herba Mystica, which normally also gives Title Power and Encounter Power for that type.

inputs.label: Sparkling Power
inputs.description: Level of the Sparkling Power meal you have active. It only applies to wild Pokémon of the meal's type.

checkpoints.label: Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 1 (4 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 2 (5 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 3 (6 rolls)

notes: Sparkling Power only applies to wild Pokémon that have the meal's type, and only to ordinary wild encounters (including Mass Outbreaks). It does nothing for Eggs, Tera Raid Battles or fixed symbol encounters.

Sparkling Power lasts 30 minutes, and eating another meal replaces it. In a sandwich, Sparkling Power only activates when at least two Herba Mystica are used (Bulbapedia, Serebii). The Indigo Disk's Academy Special (150 BP at the Blueberry Academy cafeteria) gives Sparkling Power: All Types Lv. 1, together with Catching Power Lv. 2 and Egg Power Lv. 1, without any Herba Mystica (Serebii, Bulbapedia).
The Shiny Charm is given by Jacq at the academy once the Paldea Pokédex is complete.

The Shiny Charm (+2 rolls) does not affect Tera Raid Pokémon, wild Tera Pokémon or other fixed symbol encounters, which include every wild Pokémon in the Area Zero Underdepths. Those stay at one roll; use the dedicated methods for them.
Eggs use different charm maths (2 rolls with the charm alone, not 3). Use the Breeding or Masuda Method entries for Eggs.

All static encounters (press A to start the battle), NPC gifts and NPC trades are Shiny-locked. The only exceptions are two guaranteed Shinies: the Ogre Oustin' Munchlax gift and Cyrano's Blitzle trade.
Pokémon sent out with Let's Go auto battling refuse to attack Shiny Pokémon, but that protection does not apply while using the Synchro Machine.

Resetting spawns (picnic, town border, walking away) also removes a Shiny you have not spotted, so check every wave first. If you save once a Shiny is on screen, reloading brings it back should it flee or faint.
In the Union Circle each spawn uses the Shiny bonuses of the player who caused it to appear; spawns near the host appear to use the host's bonuses (Bulbapedia).

The rates come from Anubis' datamined table for version 3.0.1, which states they are generally the same as in 1.0.1. The only later update Serebii lists, version 4.0.0 (the Nintendo Switch 2 update of June 2025), mentions just frame-rate and visual improvements in its patch notes.

methods.name: Breeding (same language)
methods.summary: Eggs from same-language parents: 1/4096, or only 2 rolls (1/2048.25) with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Breeding at a picnic with two parents that share a language of origin. Without the Shiny Charm each Egg gets a single Shiny roll. With the charm the Egg receives the charm's 2 rerolls but loses its initial roll, so it gets 2 rolls in total rather than the 3 a wild Pokémon would. Count each hatched Egg as one encounter.

checkpoints.label: Egg with Shiny Charm only (2 rolls)

notes: 8191/16777216 is the exact value of 1 - (4095/4096)^2, i.e. two rolls. It is written as a fixed case because the Shiny Charm is worth one net roll here instead of the usual two.

This is the same quirk as in Sword/Shield and Brilliant Diamond/Shining Pearl: if any reroll bonus is active, the Egg's initial roll is lost. Bulbapedia's main Shiny Pokémon table lists the Generation IX Shiny Charm as 3 rolls without separating Eggs, while Anubis' datamined table and PokéJungle give 2 rolls (1/2048.25) for charm-only Eggs; the datamined value is used.
Sparkling Power does not affect Eggs.
Switching one parent for a foreign-language Pokémon turns this into the Masuda Method (6 rolls, 8 with the charm).

methods.name: Masuda Method
methods.summary: Eggs from parents of different languages: 6 rolls (1/683.08), 8 with the Shiny Charm (1/512.44).
methods.details: Put two compatible Pokémon with different languages of origin (for example a foreign-language Ditto) in your party, set up a picnic and collect the Eggs that appear in the basket. A meal with Egg Power makes Eggs appear much faster. Every Egg from such a pair gets the Masuda Method rolls, and the Shiny Charm adds two more. Count each hatched Egg as one encounter.
notes: Internally the Masuda Method grants 6 rerolls in Generations VIII and IX, but the Egg's initial roll is skipped whenever any reroll bonus is active, so the total is 6 rolls (not 7) and 8 with the Shiny Charm (not 9). This entry models it as 1 base roll + 5 Masuda rolls, which gives the same totals.
Sparkling Power does not affect Eggs; only the Masuda Method and the Shiny Charm do.
What matters is each parent's language of origin, not the language your game is set to. Two parents with the same language tag get no bonus.
Serebii prints the rate as '6 in 4096, 1 in 682.6' (a straight multiplication); the exact value for 6 independent rolls is 1/683.08, as in Anubis' table.

methods.name: Mass Outbreak
methods.summary: Clear 60 outbreak Pokémon for +2 rolls: up to 1/512.44 with the Shiny Charm and Sparkling Power.
methods.details: Travel to an outbreak marked on the map and knock out or catch its Pokémon; Let's Go auto battles are the fastest way. Clearing 30 adds one Shiny roll and clearing 60 adds a second, and that progress is kept when you save, quit or leave the area. Once you are past 60, stop battling: open and close a picnic (or walk away and back) to respawn the group without using up the outbreak, and check each wave for a Shiny. Add a Sparkling Power meal matching the outbreak species' type and the Shiny Charm for the maximum of 8 rolls.

inputs.label: Outbreak Pokémon cleared
inputs.description: How many Pokémon of this outbreak you have knocked out or caught. Pokémon despawned by a picnic or by leaving the area do not count.

inputs.label: Sparkling Power
inputs.description: Level of the Sparkling Power meal you have active. It only helps if the outbreak species has the meal's type.

checkpoints.label: Shiny Charm + Sparkling Lv. 2, 60 cleared (7 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Lv. 3, 30 cleared (7 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Lv. 3, 60 cleared (8 rolls, best possible)

notes: Outbreak, Sparkling Power and Shiny Charm rolls simply add up: 1 base + 2 (60+ cleared) + 3 (Sparkling Lv. 3) + 2 (charm) = 8 rolls, 1/512.44, is the best possible rate.

Only knock-outs and catches of that outbreak's own Pokémon count as clears. Pokémon that despawn because you left, entered a town or opened a picnic neither count towards the bonus nor use up the outbreak, which is why picnic resets can continue indefinitely after 60.

Thresholds are exactly 30 and 60 clears per Anubis' datamine. Serebii's prose describes each step as 'between 20 and 30' Pokémon, while its own table says 30+ and 60+; the datamined values are used here.

Clearing uses up the outbreak. The game gives three warnings that the number of Pokémon is going down, and a fourth message once the Pokémon have dispersed and the outbreak is over. The warnings do not line up with the 30 and 60 thresholds, so count your clears yourself. Serebii puts the end at around 100–120 Pokémon defeated and Nintendo Life at roughly 100; the exact size is not datamine-verified here, so stop battling soon after 60.
An outbreak persists until it is cleared or until 12 a.m. real time, whichever comes first.
Sparkling Power only applies if the outbreak species has the meal's type.
Let's Go auto battling will not attack a Shiny, so clearing with it is safe.
In the Union Circle, outbreaks match the host's game and clear progress is shared by all players.

methods.name: Event Mass Outbreak (boosted)
methods.summary: Poké Portal News outbreaks with an extra flat 0.5% Shiny check: about 1/191 down to 1/144.
methods.details: During some limited-time Poké Portal News events, outbreaks of the featured species get an extra flat 0.5% Shiny check on every Pokémon that spawns. If that check fails, the normal outbreak rolls still happen, including the bonuses from clears, Sparkling Power and the Shiny Charm. Hunt it exactly like a normal outbreak: clear 60, then respawn the group with picnics and check each wave.

inputs.label: Outbreak Pokémon cleared
inputs.description: How many Pokémon of this outbreak you have knocked out or caught. Pokémon despawned by a picnic or by leaving the area do not count.

inputs.label: Sparkling Power
inputs.description: Level of the Sparkling Power meal you have active. It only helps if the outbreak species has the meal's type.

model.spec: Per-Pokémon Shiny probability for a boosted event outbreak. Inputs: defeated (number input, integer >= 0), sparkling (select input, one of 'none', 'lv1', 'lv2', 'lv3'), and whether the Shiny Charm applies (selection.shinyCharm is on, the method's charmApplies is true and the game has a charm). Constants: D = game.baseDenominator = 4096; eventChance = params.eventChance = 0.005. Steps: (1) outbreakRolls = 2 if defeated >= 60, else 1 if defeated >= 30, else 0. (2) sparklingRolls = 0 for 'none', 1 for 'lv1', 2 for 'lv2', 3 for 'lv3' (any other value counts as 0). (3) charmRolls = game.shinyCharmRolls (2) if the Shiny Charm applies, else 0. (4) rolls = 1 + outbreakRolls + sparklingRolls + charmRolls (so 1 to 8). (5) pNormal = 1 - (1 - 1/D)^rolls. (6) p = eventChance + (1 - eventChance) * pNormal. Return p as the per-Pokémon probability (rolls may be reported alongside it for the breakdown). Rationale: the game first makes a flat eventChance check; only when it fails does it make the normal rolls. Expected 1-in-N is 1/p. Reference values: rolls 1 -> 190.73, rolls 2 -> 182.29, rolls 3 -> 174.56, rolls 4 -> 167.47, rolls 5 -> 160.93, rolls 6 -> 154.88, rolls 7 -> 149.27, rolls 8 -> 144.06.

checkpoints.label: Shiny Charm + Sparkling Lv. 3, 30 cleared (0.5% + 7 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Lv. 3, 60 cleared (0.5% + 8 rolls)

notes: Only use this for event outbreaks that are announced with boosted Shiny odds. Anubis' table says event outbreaks 'can' have boosted rates and RotomLabs says they 'often' carry the 0.5% bonus, so an event without the boost follows the regular Mass Outbreak method instead.

0.5% is the bonus documented for the boosted events so far (Bulbapedia, RotomLabs; Project Pokémon's dump of the May 30 to June 1, 2025 Bug-type event also states a 0.5% Shiny rate); the rate is part of the event data, so a future event could differ.
The flat 0.5% check dominates: clears, sandwich and charm together only move the rate from 1/190.73 to 1/144.06.
Everything else works like a normal outbreak: only knock-outs and catches count, picnic resets do not deplete it, and Sparkling Power only applies if the species has the meal's type.

methods.name: Tera Raid Battles
methods.summary: Tera Raid Pokémon: a flat 1/4103.05 — the Shiny Charm and meals do not apply.
methods.details: A Tera Raid Pokémon is generated from a 32-bit seed, and 1,046,775 of the 4,294,967,296 possible seeds are Shiny, which is slightly worse than 1/4096. A Shiny raid Pokémon appears in its Shiny colours during the fight, with no sparkle or sound cue. Raid crystals are replaced at midnight or when new Poké Portal News data is received. Save before starting a raid you host: if it turns out to be Shiny you can reload and share it with other players.
notes: Raids are not affected by any bonus: not the Shiny Charm, not Sparkling Power, and Raid Power only adds item rewards.
Event Tera Raids can override this rate: some are Shiny-locked (for example the Mightiest Mark raids) and some events feature a fixed Shiny Pokémon. Check the event details.
Bulbapedia words the seed count as 4,294,967,295 while Anubis' table uses 4,294,967,296 (2^32); both round to 1/4103.05.

methods.name: Fixed symbol encounters
methods.summary: Overworld Pokémon that always appear at the same spot: a flat 1/4096 — no bonus applies.
methods.details: Fixed symbol encounters (also called wanderers) are overworld Pokémon that always appear at the same spot. They include the wild Tera Pokémon and, according to Bulbapedia, internally every wild Pokémon in the Area Zero Underdepths. They are not static encounters (you can target them with ZR or run into them to start the battle), so they can be Shiny, but they always get exactly one Shiny roll: the Shiny Charm and Sparkling Power are ignored. Count each time the Pokémon is generated as one encounter.
notes: Not affected by the Shiny Charm, Sparkling Power or outbreak bonuses.
Some fixed symbols are Shiny-locked from version 1.0.1 onward, for example the Squawkabilly on the roof of the player's house in Cabo Poco.
True static encounters (the ones where you press A to start the battle: Legendaries, ex-Titans, Gimmighoul, Snacksworth's Legendaries and so on) are Shiny-locked and cannot be hunted at all.

methods.name: Full odds
methods.summary: Wild Pokémon in Lumiose City and the Wild Zones: 1/4096, or 1/1024.38 with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Every spawner-based wild Pokémon, alphas included, rolls for Shiny when it spawns: once normally, four times with the Shiny Charm. A Shiny is visible in the overworld and announces itself with a sparkle effect and a sound. Re-roll the non-Shiny spawns by changing areas or by resting on a bench to change the time of day; at launch, repeatedly entering and leaving the tower in Wild Zone 3 was documented as an idle loop. The game keeps up to 10 uncaught Shiny Pokémon in place, so when you hear the sparkle, save and go and catch it.
notes: The Shiny Charm adds 3 rolls here (as in Legends: Arceus), not the 2 of other games. It is the reward for reaching level 50 in Mable's Research.

The base game has no other way to raise the odds; there are no per-species research levels like in Legends: Arceus. The only further boost is Sparkling Power from Mega Dimension donuts, which works only in Hyperspace.

Shiny Pokémon do not despawn when you walk away, leave the area or reload: up to 10 are stored, and an 11th replaces the oldest. You can still lose one by scaring it off or by knocking it out and failing to catch it.

Shiny-locked: the starters, Legendary and Mythical Pokémon (apart from the five Mega Dimension special scans), Rogue Mega Evolutions, NPC gifts other than fossils, in-game trades, scripted battle encounters and Pokémon that are part of a mission.
Mareep in Wild Zone 1 are Shiny-locked until you complete the side mission 'A Shiny Mareep?', which itself gives a guaranteed Shiny Mareep.
Fixed alphas that always appear at the same location are ordinary wild encounters, not static ones, and use these odds.
Shiny Pokémon get a x3 catch bonus.

The rates come from Anubis' datamined table for version 2.0.0 (the Mega Dimension update). The later versions 2.0.1 (January 2026) and 2.0.2 (March 2026) list no change to Shiny rates or the Shiny Charm in their patch notes. The Wild Zone 3 idle loop was described in October 2025 and has not been re-checked against later versions.

methods.name: Hyperspace Sparkling Power (Mega Dimension)
methods.summary: Donut Sparkling Power adds 1–3 rolls in Hyperspace Wild Zones: up to 1/585.57 with the Shiny Charm.
methods.details: Mega Dimension DLC. Have Ansha bake a donut at Hotel Z and feed it to Hoopa to turn a distortion into a portal to Hyperspace Lumiose. Donuts get random Flavor Powers, and predominantly sweet donuts are the most likely to roll Sparkling Power. While you are in a Hyperspace Wild Zone, every wild Pokémon that shares a type with the Sparkling Power (or any Pokémon, with the All Types version) gets 1, 2 or 3 extra Shiny rolls on top of the Shiny Charm's 3. With Lv. 3, the first matching Pokémon that spawns near where you enter is also forced to be Shiny.

inputs.label: Sparkling Power
inputs.description: Level of the Sparkling Power on the donut you used; Flavor Powers are random, so check each donut. It only applies to Pokémon that share a type with the power (or to all Pokémon for the All Types version).

options.label: Lv. 3
options.description: +3 Shiny rolls and one forced Shiny on arrival

checkpoints.label: Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 1 (5 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 2 (6 rolls)
Shiny Charm + Sparkling Power Lv. 3 (7 rolls, best possible)

notes: Sparkling Power is only active in Hyperspace Wild Zones and only for Pokémon that share a type with the power; it has no effect in regular Lumiose City.
Flavor Powers are random. A donut can carry up to three, at most one from each category, so the level you get is not guaranteed.

The Lv. 3 forced Shiny is not part of the odds shown here. It applies to the first Pokémon that spawns in and matches the Sparkling Power's type, and it is limited to Pokémon that spawn close to where you enter the zone. The forced Pokémon is generated with a single roll and then simply made Shiny if that roll failed; every other Pokémon keeps its full number of rolls (Anubis, RotomLabs).
The selector starts at Lv. 1, the smallest boost a Sparkling Power donut can give, because no source gives the chance of each level; set it to the level shown on your donut.
The 'Catch a Shiny Pokémon' task appears whenever any Pokémon generated on arrival is Shiny, however that happened. It is an indicator and does not cause a Shiny to spawn.
Shiny Pokémon found in Hyperspace are only kept for that portal visit; they are gone once you leave, and your time inside is limited by the donut's energy.

The special-scan Latias, Latios, Cobalion, Terrakion and Virizion count as wild encounters: they can be Shiny and benefit from the Shiny Charm and from matching or All Types Sparkling Power. Keldeo and Meloetta from the same scans are Shiny-locked.
Serebii's rate table prints '1 in 638.08' for 6 rolls and '1 in 585.37' for 7 rolls; the exact values, as in Anubis' table, are 683.08 and 585.57.

methods.name: Fossil revival
methods.summary: Revived fossil Pokémon: a flat 1/4096 — the Shiny Charm does not apply.
methods.details: Fossil Pokémon are the only gift Pokémon in Legends: Z-A that can be Shiny. Each revived fossil gets exactly one Shiny roll whether or not you own the Shiny Charm, and it also has a 1% chance to be an alpha. Count each revived fossil as one encounter.
notes: The Shiny Charm does not work on revived fossils, and Sparkling Power only applies to wild Pokémon in Hyperspace.
All other NPC gifts and in-game trades are Shiny-locked.

sandwiches.summary: A sandwich grants up to three Meal Powers for 30 minutes, each tied to one Pokémon type (Egg Power aside). Sparkling Power adds Shiny rolls for wild Pokémon of that type (Lv. 3 = 3 extra rolls) and only appears when the sandwich contains at least two Herba Mystica; the first Herba already adds Title Power (extra mark rolls). With two Herba all three powers use the sandwich's single strongest type at Lv. 3, and the recipes here steer the third power to Encounter Power, which at Lv. 3 forces every possible spawn to be that type, so nearly everything that appears gets the boosted roll. Without Herba the best solo result is Encounter Power Lv. 2 (75% of spawns forced to the type), which is enough to isolate a species but adds no Shiny rolls.

In the story it is the Herba guarded by the Stony Cliff Titan Klawf (South Province Area Three), but that one goes to Arven and never enters the Bag.

recipes.name: Normal Shiny Sandwich (Chorizo)
recipes.notes: Chorizo adds equal points to Normal, Poison, Bug, Fire, Electric and Dragon; Normal wins the tie on the game's type priority. Chorizo also gives the same three powers with Salty + Sweet, Salty + Sour or Salty + Spicy (calculator-checked). Alternative with no type tie: Tofu ×1 + Salty + Sour Herba Mystica (Game8); Tofu also gives the same three powers with Salty ×2 or Salty + Spicy (calculator-checked). Alternative from the simulator's recipe data: Rice ×1 + Salty ×2 Herba Mystica, where Normal again wins a six-way type tie.

recipes.name: Ultra Curry-and-Rice-Style Sandwich (No. 34)
recipes.notes: In-game recipe No. 34 with fixed effects (listed by Serebii and Bulbapedia); Encounter Power is its second power. No. 137 Great Tofu Sandwich (Tofu ×2, Rice, Lettuce, Avocado; Wasabi, Salt, Horseradish) lists Encounter Power: Normal Lv. 2 as its first power.

recipes.name: Fire Shiny Sandwich (Basil)
recipes.notes: Basil adds equal points to nine types (Fire, Water, Grass, Electric, Psychic, Ice, Dragon, Dark, Fairy); Fire wins the tie on the game's type priority. Two Salty Herba Mystica give Exp. Point Power as the third power instead of Encounter Power. Basil also gives the same three powers with Salty + Sour or Salty + Spicy (calculator-checked). Alternative with no type tie: Red Bell Pepper ×1 + Salty + Spicy Herba Mystica (Game8).

recipes.name: Fire Encounter Sandwich (Rice ×6)
recipes.notes: Custom Creative Mode recipe listed by Game8, shown in the Project Pokémon forum thread and included in the simulator's test data. Fire, Water and Grass tie on type points and Fire wins on the game's type priority. Cheaper variant from the community list reposted on the Project Pokémon forums (also in the simulator's recipe data): Rice ×6 + Olive Oil + Salt (Encounter Power: Fire Lv. 2, Humungo Power: Normal Lv. 2, Raid Power: Grass Lv. 1), where Fire and Grass tie and Fire wins on priority. Every piece must stay on the sandwich.

recipes.name: Water Shiny Sandwich (Cucumber)
recipes.notes: Sour and bitter tie for second flavour behind salty; sour wins on flavour priority, which keeps the bonus on Encounter Power. Cucumber also gives the same three powers with Salty + Spicy (calculator-checked).

recipes.name: Water Encounter Sandwich (Rice ×6)
recipes.notes: Custom Creative Mode recipe listed by Game8. Variant found only in the simulator's recipe data (calculator-derived): Herbed Sausage ×2 + Rice ×4 + Chili Sauce (Encounter Power: Water Lv. 2, Humungo Power: Grass Lv. 1, Exp. Point Power: Fighting Lv. 1). Every piece must stay on the sandwich.

recipes.name: Electric Shiny Sandwich (Yellow Bell Pepper)
recipes.notes: Salty and spicy tie at 500 flavour points; salty wins on flavour priority, which puts the bonus on Encounter Power. Game8's Electric page shows Salty ×2 for this recipe, but its main table, VGC, Upcomer and the simulator data all use Salty + Spicy. Two Salty Herba Mystica give Exp. Point Power as the third power instead of Encounter Power. No other Herba pair gives Encounter Power with a single Yellow Bell Pepper (calculator-checked).

recipes.name: Electric Encounter Sandwich (Noodles ×6)
recipes.notes: Custom Creative Mode recipe (no in-game recipe gives Encounter Power: Electric Lv. 2 without Herba Mystica). It is the Electric entry (6 Noodles, 1 Wasabi) of the community list of zero-Herba Lv. 2 encounter sandwiches reposted on the Project Pokémon forums and is also in the simulator's recipe data; the second and third powers are calculator-derived. Electric, Psychic and Ice tie on type points and Electric wins on the game's type priority. Variant found only in the simulator's recipe data (calculator-derived): Chorizo ×2 + Noodles ×4 + Wasabi (Encounter Power: Electric Lv. 2, Humungo Power: Psychic Lv. 1, Exp. Point Power: Poison Lv. 1); it has no type tie, but salty and hot tie at 44 flavour points and it only gives Encounter Power because salty wins that tie. Using Salt instead of Wasabi in that variant removes both ties with the same three powers (calculator-checked only, not in any published list). Every piece must stay on the sandwich.

notes: Meal Powers last 30 minutes from the moment the sandwich is made. Only three can be active, and eating another meal replaces them.
Every Meal Power except Egg Power applies to one Pokémon type only: a Sparkling Power: Dragon sandwich does nothing for spawns that are not Dragon-type.

Sparkling Power only affects ordinary wild spawns. Fixed symbol encounters (including everything in the Area Zero Underdepths), wild Tera Pokémon, Tera Raid Pokémon and Eggs do not get its extra rolls (Bulbapedia; Game8 says the same for raids and Eggs).

Sparkling Power needs at least two Herba Mystica (Bulbapedia, Serebii, Game8); a sandwich with only one never gets it. In the simulator's logic the first Herba adds Title Power and the second adds Sparkling Power, and no filling or ordinary condiment carries Title or Sparkling points (Bulbapedia's ingredient table agrees: only the Herba Mystica have them).

There are no cheaper Sparkling Power Lv. 1 or Lv. 2 recipes. Each Herba adds 250 points to every type, so a two-Herba sandwich is already Lv. 3 unless it is a failed 1-star build (13 or more pieces of one filling in solo play, per the simulator); those failed builds are the only place lower Sparkling levels appear (Game8 likewise says Lv. 2 only happens when the sandwich fails), and they still cost two Herba.

Any two Herba Mystica plus a filling give Sparkling Power Lv. 3 and Title Power Lv. 3 of the filling's strongest type; the Herba flavours only decide the third power. With a single filling the third power is whichever one receives the +100 flavour bonus, so at least one Salty Herba Mystica is needed for Encounter Power, and Salty + Bitter gives Exp. Point Power instead.

No Salty Herba Mystica? Game8's any-Herba build is Cucumber ×1, Pickle ×1 and ×3 of the type's single-type filling (Tofu, Prosciutto, Green Bell Pepper, Ham, Bacon, Cherry Tomatoes, Red Onion, Hamburger, Red Bell Pepper, Lettuce, Yellow Bell Pepper, Onion, Klawf Stick, Avocado, Smoked Fillet or Tomato; Fighting is Cucumber ×1 + Pickle ×4 and Water is Cucumber ×4 + Pickle ×1). It gives Sparkling, Title and Encounter Power Lv. 3 with any two Herba except Sweet + Sour (every type), Sweet ×2 (Normal, Fighting, Water, Bug, Dragon, Fairy) and Sour ×2 (Normal, Bug, Ghost, Ice, Dragon, Fairy), which give Catching Power instead of Encounter Power. The simulator data reproduces exactly these exceptions.

Do not drop ingredients. Every lost piece removes its points, the zero-Herba Creative Mode recipes have little or no slack (in the Rice ×6 and Noodles ×6 recipes the filling supplies exactly the 180 type points that Lv. 2 needs), and an in-game recipe that loses too many pieces turns into a custom sandwich ("A Tasty (Player) Original") whose powers are recalculated and usually weaker (Bulbapedia; the simulator treats any lost piece that way).

Quantities are servings as picked in the ingredient menu, not pieces. Solo Creative Mode allows up to ten items (Bulbapedia), which the simulator splits as 6 fillings and 4 condiments per player; Herba Mystica count as condiments, and a sandwich needs at least one filling and one condiment. Union Circle multiplayer (up to four players) allows more ingredients and stronger sandwiches, but every recipe here is solo.

Zero-Herba entries named with a recipe number are in-game recipes whose powers are fixed (Serebii's and Bulbapedia's recipe lists agree on all of them). Pick them in Recipe Mode once unlocked. According to the simulator's rules, building the same ingredients in Creative Mode with the top bread placed yields the same fixed powers, but its general formula would give these ingredient sets only Lv. 1 powers, so do not swap or drop anything.

Ties are broken by fixed priority: flavours sweet > salty > sour > bitter > hot, and types Normal > Fighting > Flying > Poison > Ground > Rock > Bug > Ghost > Steel > Fire > Water > Grass > Electric > Psychic > Ice > Dragon > Dark > Fairy (Bulbapedia; the simulator sorts in the same order). Recipes that rely on a tie-break say so in their notes.

Sources describe the level thresholds differently. Bulbapedia's community-derived table asks for a power value of 100+ and a type value of 180+ for Lv. 2, and 2,000+ and 500+ for Lv. 3 (Serebii gives the same power values). The simulator, whose author states its logic was reworked in February 2025 to match the game, sets the level from the type value alone, after the star bonus (+20 at three stars): 200+ is Lv. 2 and 400+ is Lv. 3. This file follows the simulator; it matches the published results, including Encounter Power Lv. 3 on two-Herba sandwiches, which the power-value table would not predict. The custom zero-Herba recipes here also satisfy Bulbapedia's Lv. 2 rule (power 100+, type 180+).

The top bread: Bulbapedia says leaving it off does not affect Meal Powers, while the simulator counts it as one dropped piece and only recognises in-game recipes with the bread on. Placing it is the safe choice for the zero-Herba recipes.

Which Herba flavours a Tera Raid can drop depends on the raid Pokémon (Upcomer lists Blissey, Amoonguss, Dondozo and Cetitan raids as able to drop all five). Bulbapedia's overview also lists 7★ event raids as a source. Drop rates are not included because the guides disagree.

The 18 one-filling Shiny recipes are the set published by VGC and Upcomer (VGC's Ground row omits the ×2 that Upcomer and Game8 give). Game8 lists the same recipe for 14 types and a different filling for Normal, Poison, Rock and Fire, given here as alternatives. Every recipe was re-checked with the simulator data, whose type, flavour and power values for every ingredient used in the custom recipes match Bulbapedia's ingredient table (the only difference is that Bulbapedia writes the two-Herba Sparkling bonus as 1,000 Sparkling points on each Herba).

The zero-Herba picks agree with a community list of Lv. 2 encounter sandwiches reposted on the Project Pokémon forums: it names the same in-game recipe numbers for 13 types (it uses No. 70 Ultra Refreshing Sandwich for Fighting where this file uses No. 81) and gives Noodles ×6 + Wasabi for Electric, Rice ×6 + Olive Oil + Salt for Fire and Noodles ×6 + Vinegar for Psychic.

Alternative Herba pairings marked calculator-checked were computed with a re-implementation of the simulator algorithm on its ingredient data; that re-implementation reproduces the simulator's own test recipes and Game8's published tables. The simulator's recipe files mix recipes collected online with ones produced by its own generator, so anything attributed only to the simulator's recipe data should be read as calculator-derived rather than tested in-game.
